questions.text: A student is learning Python using the interactive interpreter mode. The student issues the commands shown. What is the result?
questions.context:
>>> routers=[]
>>> switches=[]
>>> devices=["RT1", "RT2", "RT3", "SW1", "SW2", "SW3"]
>>> devices=devices + ["RT4", "SW4"]
>>> for i in devices:
      if "R" in i:
        routers.append(i)
      else: switches.append(i)
>>> switches
questions.warning: The live quiz shows the quotes in this code as \"RT1\" (with backslashes). They're ordinary quotes; the code runs as shown here.
questions.explanation: + joins the two lists, so devices holds all eight names with RT4 and SW4 at the end. The loop appends every name without an "R" to switches in order, giving SW1, SW2, SW3, SW4. Verified by running the code.

questions.text: A developer needs to check the version of the running Python package. Which command should the developer use?
questions.explanation: -V (capital V, or --version) prints the version and exits. -i enters interactive mode after running a script, -q hides the startup banner, and --v isn't a valid option (lowercase -v turns on verbose import tracing).

questions.explanation: True and False are the two Boolean values. Python reports <class 'bool'>.

questions.text: Which Python programming function is used to display output?
questions.explanation: print() sends output to the console. while, if, and for are keywords for loops and conditions, not functions.
